newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $65-$66,no trade -private.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $65-$66,no trade -private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday were lightly bid $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt, early with no trade reported, some feedlot sources said.
Other sources said buyers had not yet visited the lots nor had they called.

At $66.00, sources said cattle feeders would earn a small profit on cattle because of recent good rates and costs of gains. One source estimated steer gains averaged 3.5 to 3.6 lbs per day and heifers from 3.1 to 3.2, versus normal gains of 3.2 for steers and 3.0 for heifers.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by declines in cash beef prices since last week, sources said.
USDA quoted beef cutout values late Monday down $0.54 and $0.41 per cwt for choice cuts and up $0.21 to $0.18 for select cuts.
